# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  Lab Figure Studio
#  Upload raw assay data → publication figures → take the code home.
#
#  Run:  open this file in RStudio and click "Run App"
#        or  shiny::runApp("labviz")
#
#  Everything in R/ is auto-loaded by Shiny. Each assay is its own module,
#  so adding a new one means adding one file — nothing else changes.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# In webR/shinylive every package is baked into the bundle already, and there
# is no CRAN to install from — so only offer to install when running locally.
if (!(identical(R.version$os, "emscripten") ||
      grepl("emscripten", R.version$platform, fixed = TRUE))) {
  REQUIRED <- c("shiny", "bslib", "bsicons", "ggplot2", "scales", "ggrepel",
                "zip", "readxl")
  missing <- REQUIRED[!vapply(REQUIRED, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
  if (length(missing)) {
    message("Installing: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
    utils::install.packages(missing)
  }
}
library(shiny); library(bslib); library(ggplot2)

# Shiny draws every on-screen plot with ragg whenever it is installed, and in
# the browser that costs a 13 MB Unicode download before the first figure.
# R's own png() looks the same here, so use it.
options(shiny.useragg = FALSE)

HELPER_DIR <- normalizePath("R", mustWork = FALSE)

theme_app <- bs_theme(
  version = 5, bootswatch = "flatly",
  primary = "#0072B2",
  # A system font stack rather than Google Fonts. font_google(local = TRUE)
  # cannot download inside webR, and local = FALSE would make every visitor's
  # browser call fonts.googleapis.com — the only third-party request the app
  # would make. Dropping it means the page talks to nobody but its own origin.
  base_font    = font_collection("Inter", "-apple-system", "BlinkMacSystemFont",
                                 "Segoe UI", "Roboto", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial",
                                 "sans-serif"),
  heading_font = font_collection("Inter", "-apple-system", "BlinkMacSystemFont",
                                 "Segoe UI", "Roboto", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial",
                                 "sans-serif"),
  font_scale = 0.95
)

ui <- page_navbar(
  id = "nav",
  title = span(bsicons::bs_icon("bar-chart-line-fill"), " Lab Figure Studio"),
  window_title = "Lab Figure Studio",
  theme = theme_app, fillable = FALSE,
  header = tags$head(includeCSS("www/custom.css"), tags$script(HTML(COLOR_INPUT_JS)), tags$script(HTML(DOWNLOAD_JS)), tags$script(HTML(WIDE_JS))),

  nav_panel(
    "Start", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("house"),
    div(class = "container-lg py-3", style = "max-width: 1000px;",
      h1(class = "fw-bold mb-1", "Turn raw assay data into figures you can publish"),
      p(class = "lead text-muted",
        "Bring a spreadsheet. Leave with vector figures, statistics, and the R code behind them."),
      layout_columns(
        col_widths = c(4, 4, 4), class = "my-4",
        card(class = "h-100",
          card_body(
            h5(class = "fw-bold", bsicons::bs_icon("1-circle-fill"), " Load your data"),
            p(class = "small mb-0",
              "Upload a CSV, XLSX, or paste straight out of Excel. ",
              "You never rename a column \u2014 the app shows you its guesses and ",
              "you correct any it got wrong. Every tab has a demo file to copy over."))),
        card(class = "h-100",
          card_body(
            h5(class = "fw-bold", bsicons::bs_icon("2-circle-fill"), " Shape the figure"),
            p(class = "small mb-0",
              "Choose groups and their order, pick colours, set the comparisons ",
              "and confidence level. The figure on screen is exactly what gets ",
              "exported \u2014 no surprises at download time."))),
        card(class = "h-100",
          card_body(
            h5(class = "fw-bold", bsicons::bs_icon("3-circle-fill"), " Take it away"),
            p(class = "small mb-0",
              "PDF and SVG stay editable in Illustrator. Or take the ZIP: your ",
              "data, the analysis code, and a script that rebuilds the figures ",
              "on your own machine.")))
      ),
      h4(class = "fw-bold mt-4 mb-2", "Pick an assay"),
      layout_columns(
        col_widths = c(4, 4, 4),
        card(class = "h-100", card_body(
          h5(class = "fw-bold mb-1", "Limiting dilution"),
          p(class = "small text-muted",
            "Cells seeded and organoids counted, or wells scored +/- per dose. ",
            "Frequency bar chart with confidence intervals and significance ",
            "brackets, plus the dose\u2013response curve."),
          actionButton("go_lda", "Open", class = "btn-sm btn-primary"))),
        card(class = "h-100", card_body(
          h5(class = "fw-bold mb-1", "RT-qPCR"),
          p(class = "small text-muted",
            "A long-format Ct table becomes a \u0394\u0394Ct bar chart faceted by ",
            "gene, with tests run on \u0394Ct where they belong."),
          actionButton("go_qpcr", "Open", class = "btn-sm btn-primary"))),
        card(class = "h-100", card_body(
          h5(class = "fw-bold mb-1", "Volcano"),
          p(class = "small text-muted",
            "Any DESeq2, edgeR, or limma results table. Thresholds, gene labels, ",
            "and a hits table you can download."),
          actionButton("go_volc", "Open", class = "btn-sm btn-primary")))
      ),
      div(class = "alert alert-success border mt-4",
        h6(class = "fw-bold mb-1",
           bsicons::bs_icon("shield-lock-fill"), " Your data never leaves this computer"),
        p(class = "small mb-0",
          "This page runs R itself, inside your browser, compiled to WebAssembly. ",
          "There is no server on the other end to receive anything. Files you open ",
          "are read into this tab's sandboxed memory, and everything is discarded ",
          "when you close it. See ", strong("How it works"),
          " for how to check that claim yourself.")),
      div(class = "alert alert-light border mt-3 small",
        bsicons::bs_icon("collection"), " ",
        strong("Got a sheet with many experiments in it?"),
        " On the limiting-dilution tab, set ", strong("Split figures by"),
        " to a column such as cell line or screen. You get one figure per level, ",
        "all in a single ZIP \u2014 which is usually the actual request behind ",
        "\u201ccan you make me a figure?\u201d")
    )
  ),
  nav_panel(
    "Limiting dilution", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("circle-half"),
    layout_sidebar(sidebar = sidebar(width = 350, open = "open", ldaSidebarUI("lda")),
                   ldaUI("lda"))
  ),
  nav_panel(
    "RT-qPCR", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("thermometer-half"),
    layout_sidebar(sidebar = sidebar(width = 350, open = "open", qpcrSidebarUI("qpcr")),
                   qpcrUI("qpcr"))
  ),
  nav_panel(
    "Volcano", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("triangle"),
    layout_sidebar(sidebar = sidebar(width = 350, open = "open", volcanoSidebarUI("volc")),
                   volcanoUI("volc"))
  ),
  nav_spacer(),
  nav_panel(
    "How it works", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("info-circle"),
    card(card_body(markdown(
"## Getting your data in

Every tab accepts the same three things: the **example dataset**, an
**uploaded** `.csv` / `.tsv` / `.xlsx`, or data **pasted straight out of
Excel**. You never have to rename a column — after you upload, the app shows
a *Match your columns* panel where you point your headers at the fields it
needs. It guesses correctly most of the time.

## Limiting dilution

Two assay layouts, one model.

| Layout | You record | Model |
|---|---|---|
| **Counted organoids** | cells seeded, organoids formed | `cloglog(p) = β` — every cell is a trial |
| **Scored wells** | cells/well, wells tested, wells positive | `cloglog(p) = log(dose) + β` — classic ELDA |

Both are a binomial GLM with a complementary log-log link, so the
organoid-forming frequency is `f = exp(β)`, the confidence interval is Wald
on the log scale, and comparing two groups is a Wald test on `β_A − β_B`.
The second layout is exactly the ELDA method of Hu & Smyth (2009), written
as an offset instead of a separate function.

The **goodness-of-fit** line under the comparison table is the residual
deviance test. A small p-value means one frequency per group does *not*
explain the data — usually non-linear dose scaling, or replicates that
disagree with each other. Worth looking at before you trust the number.

## RT-qPCR

Technical replicates are averaged first. ΔCt is taken against the
housekeeping gene *within the same biological replicate*, ΔΔCt against the
mean ΔCt of the reference group, and the bar height is `2^-ΔΔCt`.

Statistics run on **ΔCt values, not fold changes** — fold changes are
log-normal, so a t-test on them is the wrong test. The p-values in the table
are Welch t-tests on ΔCt, Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted across all
gene × group comparisons.

## Volcano

Point any differential-expression table at it — DESeq2, edgeR, limma, or a
spreadsheet a collaborator emailed you. Cap the y-axis if a couple of genes
with astronomically small p-values are flattening everything else; capped
points are drawn as triangles so nobody is misled.

## Where your data goes

Nowhere. That is the whole design, not a policy promise.

This app is compiled to WebAssembly and served as plain static files. When you
open the page your browser downloads R itself — the interpreter, the graphics
devices, ggplot2, every package — and runs the entire analysis locally. There
is no R process on a server, because there is no server beyond the one that
handed you the files.

So when you upload a CSV, the browser reads it into this tab's sandboxed
memory. The bytes never travel anywhere. The same is true of anything you
paste. Figures and ZIPs are generated in the tab and handed straight to your
downloads folder. Close the tab and it is all gone — nothing is written to
disk, no cookie, no account, no log of what you analysed.

**Check it yourself**, because you should not take this on faith:

- Open DevTools (F12) → **Network**, then load a file and make a figure. You
  will see requests only while the page first loads, all to this site's own
  address, and none once R has started.
- Or simpler: load the page, turn off your wifi, and keep working. Everything
  still works, because there is nothing left to talk to.

Two things this does *not* protect against, so that the boundary is clear.
The **app** is public — anyone with the link can open it, even when the source
repository is private, unless your organisation is on GitHub Enterprise Cloud
with private Pages enabled. And anything committed to that repository is
public too, which is why real data must never be committed to it. The link
being hard to guess is not a security measure.

## Taking it with you

**A note on PDF.** On machines without a working cairo library (macOS without
XQuartz, for instance) the PDF device falls back to R's built-in one, which
cannot draw characters outside Latin-1 — a Δ or a • in a title comes out as a
dot. SVG and PNG are unaffected, so use SVG if you see that. Servers running
Linux, including shinyapps.io, have cairo and are fine.

**PDF** and **SVG** are vector — every point, line and letter stays a
separate editable object in Illustrator, Inkscape or Affinity. Use those for
papers; PNG is for slides and Slack.

The **Download data + R code** button on the limiting-dilution tab gives you
a ZIP with your data as `data.csv`, the fitting and plotting functions in
`R/`, and an `analysis.R` that rebuilds the exact figures on screen. Open it
in RStudio, hit Source, and change whatever you like. Nothing is locked
inside the app.
    ")))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$go_lda,  nav_select("nav", "Limiting dilution"))
  observeEvent(input$go_qpcr, nav_select("nav", "RT-qPCR"))
  observeEvent(input$go_volc, nav_select("nav", "Volcano"))

  ldaServer("lda", helper_dir = HELPER_DIR)
  qpcrServer("qpcr")
  volcanoServer("volc")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

# ── LDA figures ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

lighten <- function(col, amount = 0.85) {
  rgbv <- grDevices::col2rgb(col) / 255
  mix  <- rgbv + (1 - rgbv) * amount
  stats::setNames(grDevices::rgb(mix[1, ], mix[2, ], mix[3, ]), names(col))
}

# ── Panels ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lab group names usually carry two things: "Ad16-4oxoRA" is cell line Ad16
# treated with 4oxoRA. Printing twelve of those side by side under one axis is
# unreadable, so when every name splits the same way — and the second half
# repeats across the first — draw one panel per line with the treatment under
# each bar. Returns NULL when the names do not have that shape.
group_panels <- function(groups) {
  g <- as.character(groups)
  if (length(g) < 4) return(NULL)
  for (sep in c("-", "_", " | ", ": ", " ")) {
    pos <- regexpr(sep, g, fixed = TRUE)
    if (any(pos < 1)) next
    pre <- trimws(substr(g, 1, pos - 1))
    lab <- trimws(substr(g, pos + nchar(sep), nchar(g)))
    if (!all(nzchar(pre) & nzchar(lab))) next
    n_pan <- length(unique(pre))
    if (n_pan < 2 || n_pan == length(g) || !any(duplicated(lab))) next
    return(data.frame(Group = g,
                      Panel = factor(pre, levels = unique(pre)),
                      Label = factor(lab, levels = unique(lab)),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  NULL
}

use_panels <- function(groups, panels = "auto") {
  if (isFALSE(panels)) return(NULL)
  group_panels(groups)
}

# Default colours: when groups form panels, the same treatment gets the same
# colour in every panel (DMSO grey everywhere, ATRA orange everywhere).
lda_default_cols <- function(groups, palette = "Lab default") {
  p <- group_panels(groups)
  if (is.null(p)) return(pal_for(groups, palette))
  lab <- levels(p$Label)
  pl  <- pal_for(lab, palette)
  stats::setNames(unname(pl[as.character(p$Label)]), groups)
}

# Text shrinks as bars get narrower, so labels never run into each other.
label_size <- function(k) if (k <= 6) 5.4 else if (k <= 10) 4.4 else if (k <= 16) 3.6 else 3

# ── Significance marks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A handful of comparisons → brackets, stacked shortest-span first.
# More than that → stars printed above each bar (vs. the reference), because
# fifteen stacked brackets is the jumble this is trying to avoid.
MAX_BRACKETS <- 4

plan_marks <- function(comps, layout) {
  if (is.null(comps) || !nrow(comps)) return(NULL)
  comps$pi <- layout$Panel[match(comps$A, layout$Group)]
  comps$pj <- layout$Panel[match(comps$B, layout$Group)]
  comps <- comps[!is.na(comps$pi) & !is.na(comps$pj) &
                 as.character(comps$pi) == as.character(comps$pj), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(comps)) return(NULL)
  comps$Panel <- comps$pi
  comps$xi <- layout$x[match(comps$A, layout$Group)]
  comps$xj <- layout$x[match(comps$B, layout$Group)]

  per_panel <- max(table(as.character(comps$Panel)))
  if (per_panel <= MAX_BRACKETS) {
    comps$kind <- "bracket"
  } else {
    # Keep only comparisons against each panel's most-compared group.
    keep <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(comps)), as.character(comps$Panel)), function(i) {
      hub <- names(which.max(table(c(comps$A[i], comps$B[i]))))
      i[comps$A[i] == hub | comps$B[i] == hub]
    }))
    comps <- comps[sort(keep), , drop = FALSE]
    hub <- vapply(split(seq_len(nrow(comps)), as.character(comps$Panel)), function(i)
      names(which.max(table(c(comps$A[i], comps$B[i])))), character(1))
    comps$hub   <- hub[as.character(comps$Panel)]
    comps$other <- ifelse(comps$A == comps$hub, comps$B, comps$A)
    comps$x     <- layout$x[match(comps$other, layout$Group)]
    comps$kind  <- "star"
  }
  comps
}

bracket_layers <- function(marks, y0, step, tip, size = 6) {
  if (is.null(marks) || !nrow(marks) || marks$kind[1] != "bracket") return(list())
  marks$span <- abs(marks$xj - marks$xi)
  marks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(marks, as.character(marks$Panel)), function(m) {
    m <- m[order(m$span, pmin(m$xi, m$xj)), , drop = FALSE]
    m$y <- y0 + step * (seq_len(nrow(m)) - 1)
    m
  }))
  seg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(marks)), function(k) {
    r <- marks[k, ]; x1 <- min(r$xi, r$xj); x2 <- max(r$xi, r$xj)
    data.frame(Panel = r$Panel, x = c(x1, x1, x2), xend = c(x2, x1, x2),
               y = r$y, yend = c(r$y, r$y - tip, r$y - tip))
  }))
  list(
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = seg,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
      linewidth = 0.6, colour = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE),
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = marks,
      ggplot2::aes(x = (xi + xj) / 2, y = y + tip * 0.35, label = stars),
      size = size, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  )
}

star_layers <- function(marks, y, size = 5) {
  if (is.null(marks) || !nrow(marks) || marks$kind[1] != "star") return(list())
  marks$y <- y
  list(ggplot2::geom_text(data = marks,
    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = stars),
    size = size, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE))
}

# ── Bar chart ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lda_bar_plot <- function(lda, df, cols, comps = NULL,
                         title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                         show_dots = TRUE, show_labels = TRUE,
                         ylab = "Organoid-forming frequency", panels = "auto") {
  est <- lda$est
  g   <- lda$groups
  obs <- lda_observed(df[df$Group %in% g, , drop = FALSE], lda$mode)

  pan <- use_panels(g, panels)
  layout <- if (is.null(pan))
    data.frame(Group = g, Panel = factor("all"), Label = factor(g, levels = g),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  else pan
  # x position inside each panel, in the order the labels first appear
  layout$x <- ave(as.integer(layout$Label), layout$Panel,
                  FUN = function(v) match(v, sort(unique(v))))
  k <- max(table(layout$Panel))                # bars in the widest panel

  est <- merge(est, layout, by = "Group", sort = FALSE)
  obs <- merge(obs, layout, by = "Group", sort = FALSE)
  est$Group <- factor(est$Group, levels = g)

  dot_top <- if (show_dots) tapply(obs$rate, obs$Group, max) else NULL
  est$label_y <- pmax(est$CI_high,
                      if (show_dots) dot_top[as.character(est$Group)] else -Inf,
                      na.rm = TRUE)

  top   <- max(c(est$CI_high, if (show_dots) obs$rate), na.rm = TRUE)
  marks <- plan_marks(comps, layout)
  n_br  <- if (is.null(marks) || marks$kind[1] != "bracket") 0
           else max(table(as.character(marks$Panel)))
  step  <- top * 0.13
  y0    <- top * 1.20
  ymax  <- if (n_br) y0 + step * n_br
           else if (!is.null(marks)) top * 1.30 else top * 1.15

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(est, ggplot2::aes(Label, Frequency)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(fill = Group, colour = Group),
                      width = 0.6, linewidth = if (k > 10) 0.9 else 1.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high),
                           width = 0.13, linewidth = 0.9, colour = "black")

  if (show_dots)
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = obs, ggplot2::aes(Label, rate), inherit.aes = FALSE,
      shape = 21, size = if (k > 10) 2.2 else 3.2, stroke = 1, colour = "grey25", fill = NA,
      position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.07, height = 0, seed = 1))

  if (show_labels)
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(y = label_y + top * 0.04,
                   label = paste0("1/", round(1 / Frequency))),
      size = label_size(k), fontface = "bold", vjust = 0)

  p <- p + bracket_layers(marks, y0, step, step * 0.28)
  p <- p + star_layers(marks, top * 1.16, size = label_size(k))

  star_note <- if (!is.null(marks) && marks$kind[1] == "star")
    sprintf("Stars: vs %s. Every comparison is in the table.",
            paste(unique(if (is.null(pan)) marks$hub
                         else as.character(pan$Label[match(marks$hub, pan$Group)])),
                  collapse = " / "))

  p <- p +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = lighten(cols[g], 0.87), guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols[g], guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ymax),
                                expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
                  caption = star_note) +
    theme_lab() +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey35"))

  # One panel per line, each showing only its own treatments. Brackets and
  # stars use the bar's position inside its panel (layout$x), which is how a
  # free discrete scale numbers them.
  if (!is.null(pan))
    p <- p + ggplot2::facet_grid(~ Panel, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

  # Tilt the labels once, all together, they would run into each other.
  chars  <- sum(nchar(as.character(layout$Label))) + 2 * nrow(layout)
  angled <- k > 6 || chars > 32
  p + ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = if (k > 12) 11 else if (k > 6) 13 else 15, face = "bold",
      angle = if (angled) 45 else 0, hjust = if (angled) 1 else 0.5,
      vjust = if (angled) 1 else 0.5),
    strip.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.x = ggplot2::unit(1.2, "lines"))
}

# "cells" layout: organoids counted vs cells seeded, line through the origin.
# Groups that form panels get one panel each; more than six unpanelled groups
# get one small panel per group, because nine overlapping ribbons say nothing.
lda_drc_plot <- function(lda, df, cols, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                         x_step = NULL, ribbon = TRUE, panels = "auto") {
  g   <- lda$groups
  est <- lda$est
  raw <- df[df$Group %in% g, , drop = FALSE]
  raw$Group <- factor(raw$Group, levels = g)

  x_max <- max(raw$CellCount, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.06
  xs    <- seq(0, x_max, length.out = 400)
  pred  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(g), function(i) {
    data.frame(CellCount = xs, Group = g[i],
               fit   = est$Frequency[i] * xs,
               ci_lo = est$CI_low[i]    * xs,
               ci_hi = est$CI_high[i]   * xs)
  }))
  pred$Group <- factor(pred$Group, levels = g)
  y_max <- max(c(raw$Organoids, pred$ci_hi), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  if (is.null(x_step) || !is.finite(x_step) || x_step <= 0)
    x_step <- diff(range(pretty(c(0, x_max), n = 5)))[1] / 5

  pan <- use_panels(g, panels)
  facet <- NULL
  key <- "Group"; key_cols <- cols[g]
  if (!is.null(pan)) {
    raw$Panel  <- pan$Panel[match(raw$Group, pan$Group)]
    pred$Panel <- pan$Panel[match(pred$Group, pan$Group)]
    # Same treatment, same colour in every panel? Then the legend needs only
    # the treatment names — the panel title already says which line it is.
    by_lab <- tapply(unname(cols[pan$Group]), pan$Label, function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1)
    if (all(by_lab)) {
      key <- "Label"
      raw$Label  <- pan$Label[match(raw$Group, pan$Group)]
      pred$Label <- pan$Label[match(pred$Group, pan$Group)]
      key_cols <- stats::setNames(unname(cols[pan$Group[match(levels(pan$Label), pan$Label)]]),
                                  levels(pan$Label))
    }
    facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Panel, nrow = if (nlevels(pan$Panel) > 3) 2 else 1)
  } else if (length(g) > 6) {
    facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Group)
  }

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot()
  if (ribbon)
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
      data = pred, ggplot2::aes(CellCount, ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi, fill = .data[[key]], group = Group),

# "wells" layout: the classic ELDA plot — log fraction of negative wells.
lda_elda_plot <- function(lda, df, cols, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) {
  g   <- lda$groups
  est <- lda$est
  raw <- df[df$Group %in% g, , drop = FALSE]
  raw$Group <- factor(raw$Group, levels = g)
  raw$neg   <- pmax((raw$Tested - raw$Positive) / raw$Tested, 1e-3)
  raw$logneg <- log(raw$neg)

  x_max <- max(raw$Dose, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.06
  xs    <- seq(0, x_max, length.out = 200)
  pred  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(g), function(i)
    data.frame(Dose = xs, Group = g[i],
               fit = -est$Frequency[i] * xs,
               lo  = -est$CI_high[i]   * xs,
               hi  = -est$CI_low[i]    * xs)))
  pred$Group <- factor(pred$Group, levels = g)

  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = pred,
      ggplot2::aes(Dose, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = Group), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = pred, ggplot2::aes(Dose, fit, colour = Group), linewidth = 1.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = raw, ggplot2::aes(Dose, logneg, colour = Group),
                        shape = 16, size = 3.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols[g],
      guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = if (length(g) > 3) ceiling(length(g) / 3) else 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cols[g], guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, x_max),
                                expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Cells per well", y = "log fraction of negative wells",
                  title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_lab()
}

# ── Reading a protocol sheet ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# The sheets people actually keep are not tidy tables. They are blocks of
# numbers separated by blank rows, with the cell line and media written as a
# floating title above each block, no column headers, and — crucially — two
# different cell counts side by side:
#
#     Cdx2-ApcKO   R-media                  <- floating metadata, not headers
#     cells seeded                          <- a header for one column only
#     100    87    9    DMSO                <- nominal | actual | organoids | group
#     200   147   13    DMSO
#
# 100 is what the protocol said to seed. 87 is what was counted into the well.
# Fitting the model to 100 instead of 87 biases the frequency by ~20%, so the
# importer has to tell them apart rather than take the first number it sees.

# Parse a single cell to a number, tolerating "1,200", " 87 ", "300 cells".
as_num <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) return(NA_real_)
  v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9eE.+-]", "", as.character(x))))
  if (length(v) != 1 || !is.finite(v)) NA_real_ else v
}

# Words that mean "this is a column header", not "this is my experiment".
HEADER_WORDS <- paste0(
  "cell|seed|plate|organoid|colony|colonies|sphere|count|number|no\\.|#|",
  "dose|well|group|condition|treatment|sample|rep|total|formed|input")

is_header_text <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  grepl(HEADER_WORDS, x)
}

# How "round" a set of numbers is — protocol doses are 100/200/300, counted
# cells are 87/147/245.
roundness <- function(v) {
  v <- v[is.finite(v) & v > 0]
  if (!length(v)) return(0)
  max(mean(v %% 100 == 0), mean(v %% 50 == 0), mean(v %% 25 == 0),
      mean(v %% 10 == 0))
}

# ---- split a raw grid into blocks on blank rows ---------------------------
split_blocks <- function(grid) {
  blank <- apply(grid, 1, function(r) all(is.na(r) | trimws(as.character(r)) == ""))
  run <- cumsum(blank)
  idx <- split(which(!blank), run[!blank])
  Filter(function(i) length(i) >= 2, idx)     # a block needs >= 2 rows
}

# ---- classify one block ---------------------------------------------------
parse_block <- function(grid, rows) {
  b <- grid[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  nums <- suppressWarnings(
    matrix(vapply(as.matrix(b), as_num, numeric(1)), nrow = nrow(b)))

  n_num <- rowSums(is.finite(nums))
  is_data <- n_num >= 2                        # at least cells + organoids

  # Everything above the data that is pure text is the block's own label.
  lab_rows <- which(!is_data)
  label <- character()
  for (i in lab_rows) {
    vals <- trimws(as.character(unlist(b[i, ])))
    vals <- vals[!is.na(vals) & nzchar(vals)]
    vals <- vals[!is_header_text(vals)]
    label <- c(label, vals)
  }
  label <- paste(unique(label), collapse = " ")

  d <- b[is_data, , drop = FALSE]
  nm <- nums[is_data, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)

  # Numeric columns = finite in every data row. Text columns = the rest.
  num_col <- which(colSums(is.finite(nm)) == nrow(nm))
  txt_col <- setdiff(
    which(colSums(!is.na(d) & trimws(as.matrix(d)) != "") == nrow(d)), num_col)
  if (length(num_col) < 2) return(NULL)

  # The organoid column is the one that never exceeds any other numeric
  # column — you cannot form more organoids than you seeded cells.
  tot <- colSums(nm[, num_col, drop = FALSE])
  org <- num_col[which.min(tot)]
  cell_cols <- setdiff(num_col, org)

  # Of the remaining count columns, the protocol dose is the round, repeating
  # one; the real count is the noisy, near-unique one.
  score <- vapply(cell_cols, function(j) {
    v <- nm[, j]
    roundness(v) - length(unique(v)) / length(v)
  }, numeric(1))
  if (length(cell_cols) >= 2) {
    nominal <- cell_cols[which.max(score)]
    actual  <- cell_cols[which.min(score)]
  } else {
    nominal <- NA_integer_
    actual  <- cell_cols[1]
  }

  grp <- if (length(txt_col)) txt_col[which.max(vapply(txt_col, function(j)
    length(unique(trimws(as.character(d[[j]])))), integer(1)))] else NA_integer_

  out <- data.frame(
    CellCount = nm[, actual],
    Organoids = nm[, org],
    Group     = if (is.na(grp)) "ungrouped" else trimws(as.character(d[[grp]])),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  out$NominalCells <- if (is.na(nominal)) NA_real_ else nm[, nominal]
  out$Batch <- if (nzchar(label)) label else "block"

  attr(out, "cols") <- list(actual = actual, nominal = nominal,
                            organoids = org, group = grp)
  out
}

# ---- the entry point ------------------------------------------------------
# Returns a tidy data.frame plus an attached report of every decision made,
# so the app can show its working instead of asking to be trusted.
parse_protocol_grid <- function(grid) {
  grid <- grid[, colSums(!is.na(grid) & trimws(as.matrix(grid)) != "") > 0,
               drop = FALSE]
  blocks <- split_blocks(grid)
  if (!length(blocks)) stop("No blocks of data found in that sheet.")

  parsed <- lapply(blocks, function(r) parse_block(grid, r))
  keep <- !vapply(parsed, is.null, logical(1))
  parsed <- parsed[keep]
  if (!length(parsed)) stop("Found blocks, but none had two numeric columns.")

  report <- lapply(seq_along(parsed), function(i) {
    p <- parsed[[i]]; cc <- attr(p, "cols")
    data.frame(
      Block = i, Label = p$Batch[1], Rows = nrow(p),
      Groups = paste(unique(p$Group), collapse = ", "),
      `Cells column` = paste0("col ", cc$actual),
      `Protocol column` = if (is.na(cc$nominal)) "none found"
                          else paste0("col ", cc$nominal),
      `Organoids column` = paste0("col ", cc$organoids),
      check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })

  # Blocks often share a title (same line, same media) — make them distinct
  # so they can be used to split figures.
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(parsed), function(i) {
    p <- parsed[[i]]; attr(p, "cols") <- NULL; p
  }))
  labs <- vapply(parsed, function(p) p$Batch[1], character(1))
  if (anyDuplicated(labs)) {
    for (i in seq_along(parsed))
      parsed[[i]]$Batch <- sprintf("%s #%d", labs[i], i)
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parsed, function(p) {
      attr(p, "cols") <- NULL; p }))
  }
  rownames(out) <- NULL

  attr(out, "report") <- do.call(rbind, report)
  attr(out, "has_nominal") <- any(is.finite(out$NominalCells))
  out
}

parse_protocol_file <- function(path, name = path, sheet = 1) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(name))
  grid <- if (ext %in% c("xlsx", "xls")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE))
      stop("Excel files need the 'readxl' package.")
    as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = sheet, col_names = FALSE,
                                     col_types = "text", .name_repair = "minimal"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    sep <- if (ext %in% c("tsv", "txt")) "\t" else ","
    utils::read.delim(path, sep = sep, header = FALSE, colClasses = "character",
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
                      blank.lines.skip = FALSE)
  }
  parse_protocol_grid(grid)
}

protocol_sheets <- function(path, name = path) {
  if (tolower(tools::file_ext(name)) %in% c("xlsx", "xls") &&
      requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE))
    readxl::excel_sheets(path) else "1"
}

# How much would using the protocol numbers change the answer? Shown as a
# warning, because in practice it is never negligible.
nominal_cost <- function(df, groups, mode = "cells") {
  if (!any(is.finite(df$NominalCells))) return(NULL)
  d <- df[is.finite(df$NominalCells), , drop = FALSE]
  g <- intersect(groups, unique(d$Group))
  if (!length(g)) return(NULL)
  a <- tryCatch(lda_fit(d, g, mode)$est, error = function(e) NULL)
  d2 <- d; d2$CellCount <- d2$NominalCells
  b <- tryCatch(lda_fit(d2, g, mode)$est, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(a) || is.null(b)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(Group = a$Group,
             `Using counted cells` = signif(a$Frequency, 3),
             `Using protocol numbers` = signif(b$Frequency, 3),
             Difference = sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (b$Frequency / a$Frequency - 1)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}

# ── Module: RT-qPCR (ΔΔCt) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Technical replicates are averaged first; statistics are run on ΔCt values
# (never on fold changes — those are log-normal and t-tests on them are wrong).

QPCR_SPEC <- list(
  Gene      = list(label = "Gene / target", type = "character",
                   aliases = c("gene", "target", "assay", "primer", "detector")),
  Group     = list(label = "Group / condition", type = "character",
                   aliases = c("group", "condition", "treatment", "sample", "genotype")),
  Replicate = list(label = "Biological replicate", type = "character",
                   aliases = c("replicate", "biorep", "rep", "experiment", "batch")),
  Ct        = list(label = "Ct / Cq value", type = "numeric",
                   aliases = c("ct", "cq", "cycle", "ctmean", "cqmean"))
)

QPCR_EXAMPLE <- local({
  set.seed(7)
  grid <- expand.grid(Gene = c("Actb", "Lgr5", "Olfm4", "Axin2"),
                      Group = c("Control", "Treated"),
                      Replicate = c("R1", "R2", "R3"),
                      Tech = 1:2, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  base <- c(Actb = 18, Lgr5 = 26, Olfm4 = 25, Axin2 = 27)
  shift <- c(Actb = 0, Lgr5 = -1.6, Olfm4 = -2.1, Axin2 = 0.2)
  grid$Ct <- round(base[grid$Gene] +
                   ifelse(grid$Group == "Treated", shift[grid$Gene], 0) +
                   stats::rnorm(nrow(grid), 0, 0.25), 2)
  grid[, c("Gene", "Group", "Replicate", "Ct")]
})

qpcr_analyse <- function(df, hk, ref, targets) {
  # 1. collapse technical replicates
  agg <- stats::aggregate(Ct ~ Gene + Group + Replicate, data = df, FUN = mean)
  # 2. ΔCt against the housekeeping gene, within each Group × Replicate
  hkv <- agg[agg$Gene == hk, c("Group", "Replicate", "Ct")]
  names(hkv)[3] <- "Ct_hk"
  m <- merge(agg[agg$Gene %in% targets, ], hkv, by = c("Group", "Replicate"))
  if (!nrow(m))
    stop("No rows left — is the housekeeping gene measured in every replicate?")
  m$dCt <- m$Ct - m$Ct_hk
  # 3. ΔΔCt against the reference group, per gene
  refm <- stats::aggregate(dCt ~ Gene, data = m[m$Group == ref, ], FUN = mean)
  names(refm)[2] <- "dCt_ref"
  m <- merge(m, refm, by = "Gene")
  m$ddCt <- m$dCt - m$dCt_ref
  m$Fold <- 2^(-m$ddCt)
  m
}

qpcr_summary <- function(m) {
  s <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(m, list(m$Gene, m$Group), drop = TRUE), function(d) {
    n <- nrow(d)
    data.frame(Gene = d$Gene[1], Group = d$Group[1], n = n,
               Fold = mean(d$Fold),
               SEM  = if (n > 1) stats::sd(d$Fold) / sqrt(n) else 0,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  rownames(s) <- NULL
  s
}

qpcr_tests <- function(m, ref) {
  groups <- setdiff(unique(m$Group), ref)
  if (!length(groups)) return(NULL)
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(m$Gene), function(g) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(gr) {
      a <- m$dCt[m$Gene == g & m$Group == ref]
      b <- m$dCt[m$Gene == g & m$Group == gr]
      p <- if (length(a) > 1 && length(b) > 1)
             tryCatch(stats::t.test(b, a)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_) else NA_real_
      data.frame(Gene = g, A = ref, B = gr, Fold = 2^(-(mean(b) - mean(a))),
                 p = p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
  out$p_adj <- stats::p.adjust(out$p, "BH")
  out$stars <- p_stars(out$p_adj)
  out
}

qpcr_plot <- function(s, m, tests, cols, ref, title, subtitle, ylab,
                      log_y = FALSE, show_dots = TRUE, ncol = NULL) {
  s$Group <- factor(s$Group, levels = names(cols))
  m$Group <- factor(m$Group, levels = names(cols))
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(s, ggplot2::aes(Group, Fold)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(fill = Group, colour = Group),
                      width = 0.6, linewidth = 1.1) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = pmax(Fold - SEM, 0), ymax = Fold + SEM),
                           width = 0.14, linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black")
  if (show_dots)
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_point(data = m, ggplot2::aes(Group, Fold),
                                 inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 2.6,
                                 stroke = 1, colour = "grey25", fill = NA,
                                 position = ggplot2::position_jitter(0.07, 0, seed = 3))
  if (!is.null(tests) && nrow(tests)) {
    # stars sit above whichever is taller: the error bar or the highest dot
    a <- stats::aggregate(cbind(hi = Fold + SEM) ~ Gene, data = s, FUN = max)
    b <- stats::aggregate(cbind(hi = Fold)       ~ Gene, data = m, FUN = max)
    tops <- merge(a, b, by = "Gene")
    tops$top <- pmax(tops$hi.x, tops$hi.y)
    lab <- merge(tests, tops[, c("Gene", "top")], by = "Gene")
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = lab, ggplot2::aes(x = B, y = top * 1.06, label = stars),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0)
  }
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Gene, scales = "free_y", ncol = ncol) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = lighten(cols, 0.87), guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_lab(14) +
    ggplot2::theme(strip.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold.italic", size = 15),
                   panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.1, "lines"))
  if (log_y)
    p + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(trans = "log2", expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15)))
  else
    p + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA),
                                    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20)))
}

qpcrServer <- function(id) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    ns <- session$ns
    dat <- dataInputServer("d", QPCR_SPEC, QPCR_EXAMPLE)

    genes  <- reactive(sort(unique(dat()$Gene)))
    groups <- reactive(unique(as.character(dat()$Group)))

    observeEvent(genes(), {
      g  <- genes()
      hk <- g[grepl("actb|gapdh|b2m|hprt|tbp|rplp0|18s", tolower(g))]
      updateSelectInput(session, "hk", choices = g,
                        selected = if (length(hk)) hk[1] else g[1])
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

    observeEvent(list(genes(), input$hk), {
      tg <- setdiff(genes(), input$hk %||% "")
      updateSelectizeInput(session, "targets", choices = tg, selected = tg,
                           options = list(plugins = list("remove_button", "drag_drop")))
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

    observeEvent(groups(), {
      g <- groups()
      updateSelectInput(session, "ref", choices = g, selected = g[1])
      updateSelectizeInput(session, "groups", choices = g, selected = g,
                           options = list(plugins = list("remove_button", "drag_drop")))
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

    output$colour_ui <- renderUI({
      g <- req(input$groups); d <- pal_for(g, input$palette)
      lapply(g, function(k)
        colorInput(ns(paste0("col_", make.names(k))), k, value = unname(d[k])))
    })
    cols <- reactive({
      g <- req(input$groups); d <- pal_for(g, input$palette)
      stats::setNames(vapply(g, function(k) {
        x <- input[[paste0("col_", make.names(k))]]
        if (is.null(x) || !nzchar(x)) unname(d[k]) else x }, character(1)), g)
    })

    outputOptions(output, "colour_ui", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

    m <- reactive({
      req(input$hk, input$ref, input$targets, input$groups)
      d <- dat(); d <- d[d$Group %in% input$groups | d$Gene == input$hk, ]
      out <- qpcr_analyse(d, input$hk, input$ref, input$targets)
      out <- out[out$Group %in% input$groups, ]
      out$Gene <- factor(out$Gene, levels = input$targets)
      out
    })
    summ  <- reactive(qpcr_summary(m()))
    tests <- reactive(qpcr_tests(m(), input$ref))

    plot_obj <- reactive(
      qpcr_plot(summ(), m(), tests(), cols(), input$ref, input$title, input$sub,

    output$plot <- renderPlot(plot_obj(), res = 96)
    output$tbl <- renderTable({
      d <- m()[, c("Gene", "Group", "Replicate", "Ct", "Ct_hk", "dCt", "ddCt", "Fold")]
      d[, 4:8] <- lapply(d[, 4:8], function(x) round(x, 3))

    }, striped = TRUE, spacing = "s", width = "100%", align = "l")
    output$stats <- renderTable({
      t <- tests(); validate(need(!is.null(t), "Only one group — nothing to test."))
      d <- data.frame(Gene = t$Gene, Comparison = paste(t$B, "vs", t$A),
                      Fold = signif(t$Fold, 3), p = fmt_p(t$p),
                      `p adj` = fmt_p(t$p_adj), sig = t$stars, check.names = FALSE)
      as_display(d)
    }, striped = TRUE, spacing = "s", width = "100%", align = "l")
    output$csv <- downloadHandler("qPCR_ddCt.csv",

  })

# ── Module: volcano plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Takes a differential-expression results table (DESeq2 / edgeR / limma /
# anything with a fold change and a p-value) and draws a labelled volcano.

VOLC_SPEC <- list(
  Gene   = list(label = "Gene / feature", type = "character",
                aliases = c("gene", "genesymbol", "symbol", "id", "feature", "name", "x")),
  log2FC = list(label = "log2 fold change", type = "numeric",
                aliases = c("log2foldchange", "log2fc", "logfc", "lfc", "fc", "coef")),
  PValue = list(label = "p-value", type = "numeric",
                aliases = c("pvalue", "pval", "p", "praw", "pvalues")),
  padj   = list(label = "adjusted p-value", type = "numeric", optional = TRUE,
                aliases = c("padj", "fdr", "qvalue", "adjpval", "adjpvalue", "bh"))
)

VOLC_EXAMPLE <- local({
  set.seed(11)
  n <- 4000
  g <- sprintf("Gene%04d", seq_len(n))
  lfc <- stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.6)
  hit <- sample(n, 160)
  lfc[hit] <- lfc[hit] + sample(c(-1, 1), 160, TRUE) * runif(160, 1.2, 4)
  p <- stats::runif(n)^3
  p[hit] <- p[hit] / 4000
  data.frame(Gene = g, log2FC = round(lfc, 3), PValue = p,
             padj = stats::p.adjust(p, "BH"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})

volcano_prep <- function(df, use_adj, fc_cut, p_cut) {
  df$pval_used <- if (use_adj && "padj" %in% names(df)) df$padj else df$PValue
  df <- df[is.finite(df$log2FC) & is.finite(df$pval_used), , drop = FALSE]
  df$pval_used[df$pval_used <= 0] <- .Machine$double.xmin
  df$y <- -log10(df$pval_used)
  df$Status <- ifelse(df$pval_used < p_cut & df$log2FC >=  fc_cut, "Up",
               ifelse(df$pval_used < p_cut & df$log2FC <= -fc_cut, "Down", "NS"))
  df$Status <- factor(df$Status, levels = c("Down", "NS", "Up"))
  df
}

volcano_plot <- function(df, cols, fc_cut, p_cut, label_genes = character(),
                         title = NULL, subtitle = NULL, use_adj = TRUE,
                         pt_size = 1.6, alpha = 0.75, y_cap = NA,
                         show_counts = TRUE) {
  if (is.finite(y_cap) && y_cap > 0) {
    df$capped <- df$y > y_cap
    df$y <- pmin(df$y, y_cap)
  } else df$capped <- FALSE

  ylab <- if (use_adj) expression(-log[10]~italic(p)[adj]) else expression(-log[10]~italic(p))
  lim  <- max(abs(df$log2FC), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(log2FC, y)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_cut), linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = Status, shape = capped),
                        size = pt_size, alpha = alpha) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 17), guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols, breaks = c("Down", "Up")) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-lim, lim)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = expression(log[2]~fold~change), y = ylab,
                  title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_lab() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")

  if (show_counts) {
    n_up <- sum(df$Status == "Up"); n_dn <- sum(df$Status == "Down")
    ytop <- max(df$y, na.rm = TRUE)
    p <- p + ggplot2::annotate("text", x = c(-lim * 0.92, lim * 0.92), y = ytop,
                               label = c(paste0("▼ ", n_dn), paste0("▲ ", n_up)),
                               hjust = c(0, 1), vjust = 1, fontface = "bold",
                               size = 4.6, colour = c(cols[["Down"]], cols[["Up"]]))
  }

  lab <- df[df$Gene %in% label_genes, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(lab)) {
    if (requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
      p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = lab, ggplot2::aes(label = Gene), size = 3.8, fontface = "bold",
        min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.4, max.overlaps = Inf,
        segment.colour = "grey45", colour = "black", seed = 1)
    } else {
      p <- p + ggplot2::geom_text(data = lab, ggplot2::aes(label = Gene),
                                  size = 3.6, vjust = -0.8, fontface = "bold")
    }
  }
  p
}

  ns <- NS(id)
  accordion(
    open = c("1 · Data", "2 · Thresholds"),
    accordion_panel("1 · Data", icon = bsicons::bs_icon("file-earmark-spreadsheet"),
      dataInputUI(ns("d"), VOLC_SPEC, "Example DE results"),

volcanoUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)

        downloadButton(ns("png"), "PNG", class = "btn-sm btn-outline-primary"))),
    card(card_header("Significant hits"), uiOutput(ns("tbl_note")), div(class = "table-responsive", style = "max-height:480px; overflow-y:auto;", tableOutput(ns("tbl"))),
      card_footer(downloadButton(ns("csv"), "Download hits (CSV)",

volcanoServer <- function(id) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    dat <- dataInputServer("d", VOLC_SPEC, VOLC_EXAMPLE)

    prepped <- reactive({
      req(input$p_cut, input$fc_cut)
      volcano_prep(dat(), isTRUE(input$use_adj), input$fc_cut, input$p_cut)
    })

    labels <- reactive({
      d <- prepped(); sig <- d[d$Status != "NS", , drop = FALSE]
      switch(input$label_mode,
        none = character(),
        p    = utils::head(sig$Gene[order(sig$pval_used)], input$top_n),
        fc   = utils::head(sig$Gene[order(-abs(sig$log2FC))], input$top_n),
        custom = {
          g <- unlist(strsplit(input$gene_list %||% "", "[,\n\r\t ]+"))
          g <- trimws(g); g[nzchar(g)]
        })
    })

    cols <- reactive(c(Down = input$col_down, NS = input$col_ns, Up = input$col_up))

    plot_obj <- reactive({
      cap <- if (is.null(input$ycap) || input$ycap <= 0) NA else input$ycap
      volcano_plot(prepped(), cols(), input$fc_cut, input$p_cut, labels(),
                   input$title, input$sub, isTRUE(input$use_adj),
                   input$pt, input$alpha, cap, isTRUE(input$counts))
    })

    output$plot <- renderPlot(plot_obj(), res = 96)

    hits <- reactive({
      d <- prepped(); d <- d[d$Status != "NS", , drop = FALSE]
      d <- d[order(d$pval_used), ]
      keep <- intersect(c("Gene", "log2FC", "PValue", "padj", "Status"), names(d))
      d[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    })
    output$tbl <- renderTable({
      d <- hits()
      validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "Nothing passes the current thresholds."))
      for (k in intersect(c("log2FC", "PValue", "padj"), names(d)))
        d[[k]] <- signif(d[[k]], 3)
      as_display(utils::head(d, 100))
    }, striped = TRUE, spacing = "s", width = "100%", align = "l")
    output$tbl_note <- renderUI({
      n <- nrow(hits()); if (n <= 100) return(NULL)
      div(class = "form-text mb-2",
          sprintf("Showing the top 100 of %d hits by p-value. The CSV has all of them.", n))
    })
    output$csv <- downloadHandler("volcano_hits.csv",
      function(f) utils::write.csv(hits(), f, row.names = FALSE))
    dl <- function(ext) downloadHandler(paste0("volcano.", ext),
      function(f) save_plot(f, plot_obj(), input$w, input$h, input$dpi))
    output$pdf <- dl("pdf"); output$svg <- dl("svg"); output$png <- dl("png")
  })
}

# ── Downloads ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two kinds of export:
#   1. the picture (PNG / PDF / SVG — vector formats stay editable)
#   2. a ZIP holding the user's data + a standalone R script that rebuilds
#      the exact figure they are looking at, so they can keep tweaking it
#      long after they close the browser tab.

save_plot <- function(file, plot, width, height, dpi = 450) {
  dev <- tools::file_ext(file)
  if (dev == "svg") {
    # svglite is referenced by name, not as svglite::, so the web build does
    # not bundle it (it drags in ~15 MB). Locally it is used when installed;
    # in the browser R's own svg() device does the job.
    pkg <- "svglite"
    svg_dev <- if (requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE))
      getExportedValue(pkg, "svglite") else grDevices::svg
    ggplot2::ggsave(file, plot, width = width, height = height, device = svg_dev)
  } else if (dev == "pdf") {
    ggplot2::ggsave(file, plot, width = width, height = height,
                    device = pdf_device())
  } else {
    ggplot2::ggsave(file, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi,
                    bg = "white", device = png_device())
  }
}

# Turn an R value into source code that recreates it.
deparse1v <- function(x) paste(deparse(x, width.cutoff = 500), collapse = "")

# Build a directory somewhere temporary, then zip whatever ended up in it.
zip_dir <- function(zipfile, build) {
  tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("export_", as.integer(runif(1, 1e6, 1e7))))
  dir.create(tmp, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  build(tmp)
  old <- setwd(tmp); on.exit(setwd(old), add = TRUE, after = FALSE)
  files <- list.files(".", recursive = TRUE)
  # utils::zip() shells out to a zip binary, which does not exist in webR.
  # The zip package is pure C (miniz) and works everywhere.
  if (requireNamespace("zip", quietly = TRUE)) zip::zip(zipfile, files)
  else utils::zip(zipfile, files = files, flags = "-r9Xq")
}

copy_helpers <- function(tmp, helpers) {
  if (!length(helpers)) return(invisible())
  dir.create(file.path(tmp, "R"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  file.copy(helpers, file.path(tmp, "R", basename(helpers)), overwrite = TRUE)
}

# Bundle: data.csv + analysis.R + the shared helper files the script sources.
export_bundle <- function(zipfile, data, script, helpers = NULL, extra = list()) {
  zip_dir(zipfile, function(tmp) {
    utils::write.csv(data, file.path(tmp, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    writeLines(script, file.path(tmp, "analysis.R"))
    copy_helpers(tmp, helpers)
    for (nm in names(extra)) writeLines(extra[[nm]], file.path(tmp, nm))
  })
}

safe_name <- function(x) gsub("_+", "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", x))

# One figure per level of `batch_col`, plus per-level and pooled tables.
# This is the button that replaces "can you make me a figure" entirely: hand
# somebody a sheet with twenty experiments in it and they get twenty figures.
lda_batch_bundle <- function(zipfile, data, batch_col, mode, groups, cols, opts,
                             helpers = NULL, script = NULL, progress = NULL) {
  levels_ <- unique(as.character(data[[batch_col]]))
  zip_dir(zipfile, function(tmp) {
    for (d in c("Plots", "Tables", "Inputs")) dir.create(file.path(tmp, d))
    utils::write.csv(data, file.path(tmp, "Inputs", "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    copy_helpers(tmp, helpers)
    if (!is.null(script)) writeLines(script, file.path(tmp, "analysis.R"))

    all_est <- list(); all_cmp <- list(); skipped <- character()

    for (i in seq_along(levels_)) {
      lv <- levels_[i]
      if (is.function(progress)) progress(i / length(levels_), lv)
      d <- data[as.character(data[[batch_col]]) == lv, , drop = FALSE]
      g <- intersect(groups, unique(as.character(d$Group)))
      fit <- tryCatch(lda_fit(d, g, mode = mode, conf = opts$conf),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(fit) || length(g) < 1) { skipped <- c(skipped, lv); next }

      cmp <- tryCatch(
        lda_pairwise(fit, lda_pairs(g, if (opts$ref %in% g) opts$ref else g[1],
                                    opts$comp), adjust = opts$adjust),
        error = function(e) NULL)

      sub <- if (nzchar(opts$bar_sub)) paste0(opts$bar_sub, "  -  ", lv) else lv
      p_bar <- lda_bar_plot(fit, d, cols, cmp,
                            title = opts$bar_title, subtitle = sub,
                            show_dots = opts$dots, show_labels = opts$labels,
                            ylab = opts$ylab)
      p_crv <- if (identical(mode, "wells"))
        lda_elda_plot(fit, d, cols, opts$drc_title, lv)
      else
        lda_drc_plot(fit, d, cols, opts$drc_title, lv, x_step = opts$x_step)

      stem <- safe_name(lv)
      for (ext in c("pdf", "png"))
        save_plot(file.path(tmp, "Plots", sprintf("%s_frequency.%s", stem, ext)),
                  p_bar, opts$w, opts$h, 300)
      for (ext in c("pdf", "png"))
        save_plot(file.path(tmp, "Plots", sprintf("%s_curve.%s", stem, ext)),
                  p_crv, opts$w, opts$h, 300)

      est <- fit$est; est[[batch_col]] <- lv
      est$gof_p <- fit$gof_p
      utils::write.csv(est, file.path(tmp, "Tables",
                                      sprintf("%s_frequencies.csv", stem)),
                       row.names = FALSE)
      all_est[[lv]] <- est
      if (!is.null(cmp) && nrow(cmp)) {
        cmp[[batch_col]] <- lv
        utils::write.csv(cmp, file.path(tmp, "Tables",
                                        sprintf("%s_comparisons.csv", stem)),
                         row.names = FALSE)
        all_cmp[[lv]] <- cmp
      }
    }

    if (length(all_est))
      utils::write.csv(do.call(rbind, all_est),
                       file.path(tmp, "Tables", "ALL_frequencies.csv"),
                       row.names = FALSE)
    if (length(all_cmp))
      utils::write.csv(do.call(rbind, all_cmp),
                       file.path(tmp, "Tables", "ALL_comparisons.csv"),
                       row.names = FALSE)

    writeLines(c(
      "Limiting-dilution batch export",
      paste("Generated:", format(Sys.time())),
      paste("Split by:", batch_col),
      paste("Levels:", length(levels_)),
      if (length(skipped))
        paste("Skipped (model would not fit):", paste(skipped, collapse = ", ")),
      "",
      "Plots/   one frequency bar chart and one curve per level (PDF + PNG)",
      "Tables/  per-level frequencies and comparisons, plus pooled ALL_* files",
      "Inputs/  the data exactly as it was analysed",
      "R/       the fitting and plotting functions",
      "analysis.R  rerun or edit everything in RStudio",
      "",
      "PDF is vector: every element stays editable in Illustrator or Inkscape.",
      "gof_p in the frequency tables is the goodness-of-fit p-value; small",
      "values mean one frequency per group does not describe that level well."
    ), file.path(tmp, "README.txt"))
  })
}

lda_script <- function(mode, groups, cols, opts) {
  helper_files <- c("00_theme.R", "02_lda_stats.R", "03_lda_plots.R")
  paste0(
'# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  Limiting-dilution analysis — reproducible script
#  Generated by the lab figure app on ', format(Sys.Date()), '
#
#  HOW TO USE
#    1. Keep this file next to data.csv and the R/ folder.
#    2. Open in RStudio and hit Source. Figures land in figures/.
#    3. Everything below is plain ggplot2 — change anything you like.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

library(ggplot2); library(scales)
for (f in list.files("R", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)

df   <- read.csv("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
mode <- "', mode, '"

groups <- ', deparse1v(groups), '
cols   <- ', deparse1v(cols), '

# ── Fit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lda <- lda_fit(df, groups, mode = mode, conf = ', opts$conf, ')
print(lda$est)

# ── Group comparisons (Wald on the log-frequency scale) ────────────────
pairs <- ', deparse1v(opts$pairs), '
comps <- lda_pairwise(lda, pairs, adjust = "', opts$adjust, '")
print(comps)

# ── Figures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

p_bar <- lda_bar_plot(lda, df, cols, comps,
                      title    = ', deparse1v(opts$bar_title), ',
                      subtitle = ', deparse1v(opts$bar_sub), ',
                      show_dots = ', opts$dots, ', show_labels = ', opts$labels, ',
                      ylab = ', deparse1v(opts$ylab), ')
ggsave("figures/LDA_frequency.pdf", p_bar,
       width = ', opts$w, ', height = ', opts$h, ', device = pdf_device())

p_curve <- ', if (mode == "cells")
  paste0('lda_drc_plot(lda, df, cols,
                     title    = ', deparse1v(opts$drc_title), ',
                     subtitle = ', deparse1v(opts$drc_sub), ',
                     x_step   = ', opts$x_step, ')')
else
  paste0('lda_elda_plot(lda, df, cols,
                      title    = ', deparse1v(opts$drc_title), ',
                      subtitle = ', deparse1v(opts$drc_sub), ')'), '
ggsave("figures/LDA_curve.pdf", p_curve,
       width = ', opts$w, ', height = ', opts$h, ', device = pdf_device())

write.csv(lda$est, "figures/frequencies.csv", row.names = FALSE)
if (!is.null(comps)) write.csv(comps, "figures/comparisons.csv", row.names = FALSE)
')
}

content:
# Lab Figure Studio

A Shiny app that turns raw assay spreadsheets into publication figures, and
hands the user back the data and the code.

Three assays, one interface:

| Tab | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| **Limiting dilution** | cells seeded + organoids counted, *or* wells scored +/- per dose | frequency bar chart with CIs and significance brackets, dose–response / ELDA curve, frequency and comparison tables |
| **RT-qPCR** | long-format Ct table | ΔΔCt bar chart faceted by gene, Welch tests on ΔCt |
| **Volcano** | any DE results table | labelled volcano, hits table |

## Run it

```r
shiny::runApp("labviz")
```

Or open `app.R` in RStudio and click **Run App**. Missing packages install on
first launch.

## Batch mode

The button that actually gets you out of the loop. On the limiting-dilution
tab, set **Split figures by** to a column such as cell line, screen, or
timepoint. The app then writes one frequency chart and one curve *per level*
into a single ZIP:

```
Plots/    HT29_frequency.pdf/.png, HT29_curve.pdf/.png, LS174T_..., SW480_...
Tables/   per-level frequencies + comparisons, plus pooled ALL_*.csv
Inputs/   the data exactly as analysed
R/        the fitting and plotting functions
analysis.R, README.txt
```

Levels whose model will not fit are skipped and named in `README.txt` rather
than failing the whole export. Borrowed from Metabolite AutoPlotter
(Pietzke & Vazquez 2020), which does the same thing one-plot-per-metabolite.

## Protocol sheets

Real lab sheets are not tidy tables. The importer under **Protocol sheet** on
the limiting-dilution tab reads one as written: blocks separated by blank
rows, the cell line and media floating above each block as a title, no column
headers, and no consistent ordering.

It works out which column is which from the numbers themselves:

- the **organoid** column is the one that never exceeds any other count —
  you cannot form more organoids than you seeded cells
- the **protocol** column is round and repeating (100, 200, 300, 400)
- the **counted** column is noisy and near-unique (87, 147, 245, 337)

That last distinction is the point of the feature. A sheet that records both
what you meant to seed and what you actually counted will give frequencies
roughly 20% too low if the model is fitted to the protocol number. The
importer defaults to the counted column, says so, and puts a table on the
figure tab showing exactly what the other choice would do to every group.

Verified against `LDA 0514.xlsx`: two blocks, seven groups, all seven
frequencies reproduced to seven significant figures from the untouched
workbook.

## Layout

```
labviz/
├── app.R                  # navbar + wiring, nothing else
├── R/                     # auto-sourced by Shiny
│   ├── 00_theme.R         # ggplot theme, palettes, p-value stars
│   ├── 01_io.R            # upload / paste / column-mapping module
│   ├── 02_lda_stats.R     # the cloglog GLM
│   ├── 03_lda_plots.R     # bar + curve + ELDA figures
│   ├── 10_mod_lda.R       # ┐
│   ├── 20_mod_qpcr.R      # ├ one Shiny module per assay
│   ├── 30_mod_volcano.R   # ┘
│   └── 40_export.R        # PNG/PDF/SVG + the reproducible-code ZIP
└── www/custom.css
```

Adding a fourth assay means adding one `R/` file with a `*SidebarUI`, `*UI`
and `*Server`, then three lines in `app.R`. Nothing else changes.

The statistics and plotting files (`00`, `02`, `03`) are deliberately free of
any Shiny dependency — they are plain functions. That is what lets the export
button ship them to the user as a working standalone script.

## Deploying to GitHub Pages

The app is built to WebAssembly and served as static files, so there is no
server to run, nothing to pay for, and no R process anywhere that could
receive lab data.

Push this directory to a repo and let CI do the build — `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
is already written. In the repo, **Settings → Pages → Source → GitHub Actions**,
then push to `main`. The action installs the packages, runs
`shinylive::export("labviz", "_site")`, and publishes. The build takes a few
minutes; the resulting site is about 106 MB, well inside the 1 GB Pages limit.

`docs/` and `_site/` are gitignored on purpose. Committing a 100 MB build
output bloats the repo and lets the deployed app drift from the source — let
the action rebuild it every push.

To build and check it locally before pushing:

```r
shinylive::export("labviz", "docs")
httpuv::runStaticServer("docs", port = 8008)
```

Note that a service worker is required, so `file://` will not work — you need
a real local server, and some embedded browsers block service workers
entirely. Chrome, Firefox and Safari are all fine.

### Verified WebAssembly compatibility

Every package the app uses is available for webR, and three things were
changed so the app works in the browser:

| Problem in webR | Fix |
|---|---|
| `utils::zip()` shells out to a `zip` binary that does not exist | `zip::zip()` — pure C, no shell |
| `png()` wants cairo/X11 | `ragg::agg_png()` |
| `install.packages()` at startup; `font_google()` fetches from Google | skipped under Emscripten; system font stack |

The exported bundle is genuinely self-contained. `library.data.gz` (15 MB)
carries shiny, bslib, htmltools, sass and 32 more; `shinylive/webr/packages/`
carries the other 39, including ggplot2, DT, svglite, colourpicker and ragg.
Nothing is fetched from `repo.r-wasm.org` or any other third party at runtime,
and after the swap above there are no requests to Google Fonts either — the
page talks only to its own origin.

## Security

The privacy property is architectural, not a promise: uploaded data is read
into the browser tab's sandboxed memory and analysed by an R interpreter
running in that same tab. There is no server-side session to leak, because
there is no server-side session.

Anyone can verify it in under a minute — DevTools → Network shows requests
only while the page loads, none afterwards; or load the page, disconnect from
the network, and keep working.

Two real limits, stated plainly:

- **GitHub Pages is public.** On Free, Pro and Team accounts the published
  site is world-readable even when the source repo is private; private Pages
  needs GitHub Enterprise Cloud (Settings → Pages → Visibility → Private).
  This is fine here — the *app* being public costs nothing, because the *data*
  never goes there. But do not treat an unguessable URL as a control.
- **Never commit real data.** The `.gitignore` blocks `*.csv`, `*.tsv`,
  `*.xlsx`, `*.rds` and `.RData` for that reason. The example datasets are
  synthetic and defined inline in `R/`, so there is no data file to whitelist.

## Notes on the statistics

Limiting dilution uses a binomial GLM with a complementary log-log link.
Both supported layouts are the same model; the well-scoring layout is the ELDA
method of Hu & Smyth (2009, *J Immunol Methods* 347:70) expressed as an
`offset(log(dose))`. Frequencies are `exp(β)`, intervals are Wald on the log
scale, group comparisons are Wald tests on `β_A − β_B`.

The residual-deviance goodness-of-fit p-value is shown under the comparison
table. Treat a small value as a warning that one frequency per group does not
describe the data — usually non-linear dose scaling or disagreeing replicates.

qPCR statistics run on ΔCt values, never on fold changes.
